title: Cult 80s
blurb: The ones that flopped in theatres and lived forever on the rental shelf. Sorcerers in Chinatown, a satire in a steel suit, an alligator in the sewers, and Turkish Star Wars.

films.note: John Carpenter, Kurt Russell and a Chinatown full of sorcerers. It flopped in 1986 and has been a midnight movie ever since.
Paul Verhoeven's satire of corporations, cops and TV ads, dressed up as an action film.
Weird Al Yankovic takes over a failing TV station. A box-office miss that found its audience on video.
A flushed baby alligator grows up in the sewers. Written by John Sayles, who knew exactly what film he was making.
Turkish Star Wars. Borrowed footage, borrowed music, total conviction.
Steve Martin plays opposite Bogart, Stanwyck and Cagney, spliced in from forties noir.
A seaside town where the tourists keep dying and the locals keep smiling. From the writers of Alien.
A UFO cover-up from Sunn Classic Pictures, who made a business of this sort of thing.
Sketch comedy shaped like a night of channel-surfing, from five directors including Joe Dante and John Landis.
Small-town teenagers, a mad scientist, and a Tangerine Dream score.
Michele Soavi's debut: a theatre locked for the night, with a killer in an owl mask.
Godfrey Ho's cut-and-paste ninja cinema, the kind only the eighties could make.
